uncited: Regularization and Loss Functions define the objective landscape for optimizing Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) during differentiable volume rendering.

While the parent [NeRF Training Loop](970-nerf-training-loop.md) handles sampling strategies to balance training data, this family addresses the ill-posed nature of the inverse rendering problem by enforcing geometric plausibility, structural coherence, and semantic consistency beyond simple pixel-wise photometric reconstruction.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Training Ray Marching and Integration](2199-training-ray-marching-and-integration.md) by focusing on the *what* to optimize (the loss terms and regularizers) rather than the *how* of the integration process.

- **Steps**: Supervise cache diffuse color $c_{\text{cache}}(\mathbf{x})$ and specular color $c_{\text{cache}}(\mathbf{x}, \omega_i)$ to match physically-based model colors $c_{\text{phys}}(\mathbf{x})$ and $c_{\text{phys}}(\mathbf{x}, \omega_i)$.
- **Definition**: A loss function using saturation values from a reference image to constrain the generated object, mitigating color over-saturation issues.

The rendering process computes expected color and depth along rays $r(t) = o + td$ using sample points $t_i$ with weights $w_i = T(t_i)\rho(t_i)$, where $\rho(t_i) = 1 - \exp(-\sigma(\mathbf{r}(t_i))(t_{i+1} - t_i))$ and $T(t_i) = \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \rho(t_j))$ [S1].
